solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It could be grand over the Styx, we hear

definitions.text: It could be grand over the Styx, we hear

parts.words: It could be grand over the Styx, we hear
parts.note: Styx said aloud is 'sticks', the jumps of a steeplechase

explanation.surface: A grand journey across the mythical river of the underworld, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Styx is a red herring: spoken, it is 'sticks', racing slang for steeplechase fences. The Grand National is a famous British horse race over fences at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand is the word that famously precedes this one in the name of the steeplechase, so a grand race over fences fits.

clue.text: Record two males a long time, one lasting only a day

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
HE is a male pronoun and M the abbreviation for male
HE is a male pronoun and M the abbreviation for male
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A record-keeping note about two men spending ages with something short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayfly genus gives its name to things that live a single day, and the word covers any short-lived creature or item.

clue.text: Princess got married initially taking a step forward to be attached

parts.note: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal

indicators.note: the first letter moves one step on in the alphabet, so its initial is replaced by the following letter

parts.note: wed means got married

explanation.surface: A royal wedding where the princess steps forward to be joined to her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially taking a step forward' moves the W of WED one place along the alphabet, making XED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annexed has been joined on or appended, a synonym of attached.

clue.text: Itching for honour after partners take the lead

indicators.note: the honour card comes after the partners, who take the lead at the front

parts.note: East and West are partners at the bridge table
in bridge the king is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: Someone itching for a title once their partners have gone first.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridge clue: East-West are a partnership and the king is an honour card. 'take the lead' confirms the partners go first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewk or yeuk is a Scots and northern dialect verb for itch, so this is a dialect form of itching.

clue.text: This is necessary for a junket

definitions.text: This is necessary for a junket

parts.words: This is necessary for a junket
parts.note: junket here is not a jolly trip but a milk pudding set with a curdling agent from a calf's stomach

explanation.walkthrough: A junket usually means a free trip, but it is also a sweet set milk dessert, which needs the curdling agent to set.
explanation.definitionFit: The curdling enzyme from a calf's stomach is the essential ingredient that sets milk into the dessert called junket.

clue.text: Anyway he appears not as drunk as you might wish him

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling about into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, used as written
the letters of this word are the ones the fodder has to lose, as 'not' says

explanation.surface: A reveller who turns up less drunk than his friends would have liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not as' means the letters A and S are taken from ANYWAY HE APPEARS before 'drunk' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Year greeting is what you wish someone at midnight on the thirty-first of December.

clue.text: One not voting for party driver

definitions.meaning: someone who abstains from casting a vote
the person at a party who abstains from drink because they are driving home

explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer declines to vote, and the designated driver at a party also abstains, from alcohol.

clue.text: Moving location for food and drink

definitions.text: Moving location for food and drink

parts.words: Moving location for food and drink
parts.note: a place to eat and drink that is itself travelling, being one carriage of a train

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests relocating a cafe; in fact the eatery is in motion, as a carriage on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining carriage on a train serves meals and drinks while the train moves along.

clue.text: Hope to be seen at church …

definitions.meaning: to hope is to long for or aim at something
read as two words, a tall pointed steeple is visible on a church

explanation.definitionFit: To aim for something is to hope for it, and split in two the word gives a steeple, a feature of a church.

clue.text: … for sin in selves to be freed

indicators.note: letters set free from their order are loose to fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue above: hoping for wickedness within ourselves to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 8 across, making one sentence of the two clues. 'to be freed' rearranges IN SELVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sin and wickedness are near synonyms for moral badness.

clue.text: In Rome, ha!

parts.note: ha is an abbreviation of the Latin hoc anno, in this year, and in Rome the year is written in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: 'ha' looks like a laugh, but h.a. is short for Latin hoc anno, 'in this year'. The puzzle appeared for New Year 2010, which Romans would write in numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numerals for two thousand and ten give the year current when the puzzle was published.

clue.text: Head that is covering

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Reads like a dictionary entry for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small close-fitting knitted cap is a covering for the head.

clue.text: Hay diet's good for upset lasting more than a week

indicators.note: an upset overturns things, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A slimming regime that sounds good for a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight days is longer than a week, as with an old clock that runs for over a week on one winding.

clue.text: She never has to lose resolution in Scotland

indicators.note: the first two words have, or contain, the letters across their join

explanation.surface: A woman who never needs to give up her New Year resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' tempts as the definition (a hen is a female); but here the word is the Scots verb meaning to lose one's nerve or back out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, the verb hen means to funk or lose one's courage, so it fits losing resolution.

clue.text: Like a star fish about to relate

indicators.note: the fish goes about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: the sar is a sea bream, a fish familiar in crosswords
to tell is to relate a story

explanation.surface: Describing a starfish, a fish about to tell a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective from the Latin word for a star describes anything relating to or like one.

clue.text: Ley line near water

parts.note: ea is an old and dialect word for a river or watercourse

explanation.surface: A mystical ley line that runs close to some water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ley line' looks like one phrase, but 'Ley' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ley is a variant spelling of the poetic word for a meadow or grassland.

clue.text: Working in time to be announced today

indicators.note: the working word sits inside the time word

parts.note: hours are units of time
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Someone at work waiting in good time for news due today.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on New Year's Day, when the British New Year Honours list of awards is published.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Year awards list of knighthoods and medals is announced on the first of January.

clue.text: Starts to dance, but most people don't do this today

definitions.text: most people don't do this today

parts.note: opens means starts or begins
to hop is to dance, as at a dance called a hop

explanation.surface: Someone starting to dance while everyone else stays at home.
explanation.definitionFit: On New Year's Day most businesses close, so trading as usual is something few do.

clue.text: Expressing a desire to choose musical to return

parts.note: opt means choose

indicators.note: a musical's return here means its title is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: Wanting to pick a show that comes back to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical mood that expresses a wish, as in Greek, is the wishing mood.

clue.text: Twice a year swig wine, initially getting drunk, but the end result is the same

definitions.text: the end result is the same

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word wine
getting drunk sends the collected letters reeling into a new order
twice means the year abbreviation is used two times

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Drinking wine twice a year and getting tipsy, with the same outcome each time.
explanation.definitionFit: The computing acronym means what you see is what you get: the printed result matches the screen.

clue.text: Yesterday lots of people got round a pig for starters

parts.note: a hog is a pig, and 'for starters' says it goes at the front

indicators.note: the crowd got round, or surrounded, the single letter

parts.note: many means lots of people

explanation.surface: A crowd gathering round a hog roast for the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on New Year's Day, so the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration was yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish name for the thirty-first of December was the day before this New Year's Day puzzle.

clue.text: It could be over with May in French nightclub

parts.note: Mai is French for the month of May
a den is a dive or haunt, such as a seedy nightclub

explanation.surface: A night out at a club in France in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, and one with no runs scored is a maiden over.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over in which no runs are scored is called a maiden, so an over could be one.

clue.text: More effective to have meal in north-eastern region at first

indicators.note: the eating goes in the middle of the compass abbreviation

parts.note: to eat is to have a meal

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of region

explanation.surface: Dining in the North East is said to be more efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can mean skilful and efficient, as in a neat solution, so the comparative fits more effective.

clue.text: Tagine perhaps the object of seasonal activity

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A North African stew served as part of the festive feasting.
explanation.walkthrough: A tagine is a Moroccan stew; it is itself something to eat, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasting at Christmas and New Year is the main purpose of much seasonal activity.

clue.text: Paper for Jan 3?

definitions.meaning: the third of January 2010 fell on a Sunday, abbreviated to its first three letters

explanation.definitionFit: A British tabloid shares its name with the abbreviation of the weekday that 3 January 2010 fell on.

clue.text: Return independent woman: any different one will be a dish

indicators.note: return means the first two pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: rib is a jocular word for a woman, from Adam's rib

indicators.note: different signals the three letters of any in another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A self-reliant woman tells someone to send back an unwanted plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns I RIB into BIRI; 'different' makes YAN from ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiced rice dish from South Asia is a well-known example of a dish.

clue.text: It's the familiar routine: hush money advanced

parts.note: sh is a call for hush
tick is credit, money lent in advance of payment

explanation.surface: A routine where someone pays quiet money up front.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's habitual gimmick or act is their stock routine, an informal Yiddish-derived word.

clue.text: In turbulent love story always for each of you

indicators.note: in places the word for always inside the scrambled story
turbulent shakes up the letters of the story into a new order

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A stormy romance that goes on for ever, addressed to every reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' shuffles LOVE STORY, and 'In' puts the word for always inside the result; the definition is the setter's greeting to readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's message is addressed to every person tackling the puzzle, so it means to each of you.
